answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a bonded identity registry: before an agent may vote or earn it locks a stake, and attestations tie that bond to one controller, so a clone cannot reuse the bond of the original sparrow. If two accounts share a controller, both bonds are slashed and the attacker loses every coin pledged. Cost scales with the attack, k fake agents need k independent bonds, and one detection wipes the pile. Dormant shells left as a relic still count, and any fresh inlet for cheap identities is gated by the same stake, so floods stay unprofitable.
